literal: Even if they speak things devoid of pleasantness, let the noble people speak them; but not speaking things devoid of usefulness is good.
translation: Even if noble people speak words devoid of pleasantness, it is still better for them to completely refrain from speaking words devoid of usefulness.
modern: சான்றோர்கள் அறநெறி அல்லது இனிமை இல்லாத சொற்களைச் சொன்னாலும் சொல்லலாம்; ஆனால், பயனில்லாத சொற்களைச் சொல்லாமல் இருப்பது அவர்களுக்கு மிகவும் நல்லது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute necessity of avoiding useless chatter by comparing it with unpleasant speech. The author suggests that even if wise and noble people (சான்றோர்) happen to utter words lacking in pleasantness or virtue (நயனில), it may be tolerated. However, it is of paramount importance and goodness (நன்று) that they never speak words that are completely devoid of utility or purpose (பயனில). This comparison emphasizes that while harsh or unvirtuous words might occasionally occur under specific circumstances, useless words serve no purpose at all and must be strictly avoided.
